eips.title: Fork-choice enforced Inclusion Lists (FOCIL)
eips.summary: Entire call centered on FOCIL's post-quantum transition, Hegota scoping, and whether to defer or ship it alongside frames.

moments.context: Jihoon opened the call noting a proposal to defer FOCIL from Hegota in favor of going all-in on PQ consensus, with a final decision expected on the December 10 ACDC call.

soispoke presented slides breaking PQ FOCIL into two parts: PQ-signed transactions fitting in ILs (feasible now, ~1 per IL) and ILs themselves carrying PQ signatures or STARK proofs (much harder, deferred).
soispoke argued that 16 committee members each including one PQ transaction per slot is sufficient initially, before aggregation exists.
soispoke discussed replacing BLS IL signatures with lean XMSS, adding 2.4 KB per IL, arguing it is not urgent because attacking FOCIL via quantum is impractical compared to attacking consensus.
soispoke noted that shipping FOCIL alongside frames will cause some delay but argued it would not necessarily delay the PQ I-star fork given how far away PQCL work is.
Jihoon suggested delaying IL enforcement to slot n+2 instead of n+1 to gain 12 more seconds of propagation time for large STARK proofs, acknowledging it sacrifices a core EIP-7805 design value.
Justin Florentine questioned whether dropping FOCIL from Hegota would actually save meaningful time given FOCIL is already far along and PQCL decisions remain unresolved.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: Discussed extensively as the dependency enabling PQ transaction aggregation on the EL and eventual STARK-based ILs for FOCIL.

moments.context: soispoke said FOCIL can include individual PQ transactions now but needs EIP-8288 aggregation before ILs can carry STARK proofs at scale.
Mikhail asked how likely PQ EL would ship without 8288; soispoke said quite likely because users will want leanSPHINCS signatures before leanVM is ready.
soispoke outlined three phases of 8288: leanSPHINCS (possibly H-star), mempool recursive aggregation via leanVM (I-star target, ~mid-2028), and leanPCS arbitrary proofs (I-star or J-star).

Mikhail asked whether after 8288 the mempool would have only STARK batches; soispoke clarified that raw-signature transactions would still exist on first hop, allowing FOCIL includers to pick them up.
soispoke acknowledged that figuring out what FOCIL looks like post-8288 and post-PQCL is impossible today but worth exploring in each scenario.
Marc said breaking 8288 into sub-EIPs simplifies reasoning and that the interaction between FOCIL and aggregation will be the hardest part.
